## Predominance Condition

(1) A state with initial thought and sustained thought is related to a state with initial thought and sustained thought by way of predominance condition (Adhipatipaccaya): there are two kinds, namely, object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati) and conascence-predominance (sahajātādhipati). Object-predominance: having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the Uposatha duties, one reviews them, giving weight to them. One reviews former good deeds well performed, giving weight to them. ## Ārammaṇapaccayo
A state accompanied by rapture is related to a state accompanied by rapture by way of object condition: having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the Uposatha duty with a mind accompanied by rapture, one reviews that gift etc. with a mind accompanied by rapture. Having emerged from absorptions accompanied by rapture, having emerged from the paths, having emerged from the fruitions, one reviews those absorptions, paths, and fruitions with a mind accompanied by rapture. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements accompanied by rapture with a mind accompanied by rapture; they review the suppressed defilements; they know the defilements previously practiced. They contemplate the aggregates accompanied by rapture with a mind accompanied by rapture as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self; they enjoy and delight in them. Depending on those aggregates, lust accompanied by rapture arises, wrong view arises. Depending on the aggregates accompanied by rapture, aggregates accompanied by rapture arise. (1)

A state accompanied by rapture is related to a state accompanied by happiness by way of object condition: having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the Uposatha duty with a mind accompanied by rapture, one reviews that act with a mind accompanied by happiness. Having emerged from absorptions accompanied by rapture, having emerged from the paths, having emerged from the fruitions, one reviews those states with a mind accompanied by happiness. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements accompanied by rapture with a mind accompanied by happiness; they review the suppressed defilements; they know the defilements that occurred in the past. A state accompanied by rapture is related to a state accompanied by equanimity by way of object condition: having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the Uposatha duty with a mind accompanied by rapture, one reviews that act with a mind accompanied by equanimity. They contemplate the aggregates accompanied by rapture with a mind accompanied by equanimity as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self; they enjoy and delight in them. Depending on those aggregates accompanied by rapture, lust accompanied by equanimity arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises. By the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, they know the mind of one possessed of a mind accompanied by rapture. Aggregates accompanied by rapture are related to the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, to the knowledge of recollection of past lives, to the knowledge of beings passing away according to their kamma, to the knowledge of the future, and to adverting by way of object condition. ## Ārammaṇapaccayo
An ācayagāmī dhamma is related to an ācayagāmī dhamma by way of object condition: after giving a gift, undertaking virtue, or performing the Uposatha observance, one reflects on that merit; one reflects on previously well-performed wholesome deeds; after emerging from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna. Sekhas reflect on abandoned defilements, reflect on suppressed defilements, and know the defilements that frequently occurred in the past. Sekhas or worldlings gain insight into ācayagāmī aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they enjoy and delight in them; taking those ācayagāmī aggregates as object, lust arises, views... pe... doubt... pe... restlessness... pe... grief arises; they know the mind of one possessed of an ācayagāmī mind through the knowledge of others' minds; ākāsānañcāyatana-wholesome is related to viññāṇañcāyatana-wholesome by way of object condition. Ākiñcaññāyatana-wholesome is related to nevasaññānāsaññāyatana-wholesome... pe... ācayagāmī aggregates are related to the knowledge of supernormal powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and the knowledge of the future by way of object condition. (1)

An ācayagāmī dhamma is related to a nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma by way of object condition: an Arahant reflects on abandoned defilements, knows the defilements that frequently occurred in the past, gains insight into ācayagāmī aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, and knows the mind of one possessed of an ācayagāmī mind through the knowledge of others' minds. Sekhas or worldlings gain insight into ācayagāmī aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; when the wholesome consciousness ceases, resultant registration (tadārammaṇa) arises; they enjoy and delight in ācayagāmī aggregates; taking those ācayagāmī aggregates as object, lust arises... pe... grief arises; when the unwholesome consciousness ceases, resultant registration arises; ākāsānañcāyatana-wholesome is related to viññāṇañcāyatana-resultant and functional by way of object condition. Ākiñcaññāyatana-wholesome is related to nevasaññānāsaññāyatana-resultant and functional by way of object condition. Ācayagāmī aggregates are related to the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and adverting (āvajjana) by way of object condition. (2)

An apacayagāmī dhamma is related to an ācayagāmī dhamma by way of object condition: Sekhas emerge from the Path and reflect on the Path; through the knowledge of others' minds...

(Others) know the mind of one possessed of the mind leading to the cessation of rebirth (apacayagāmī); the aggregates leading to the cessation of rebirth are a condition for the knowledge of others' minds (cetopariyañāṇa), the knowledge of recollection of past lives (pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa), and the knowledge of the future (anāgataṃsañāṇa) by way of object condition. (1)

A state leading to the cessation of rebirth is a condition for a state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation (nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī) by way of object condition: An Arahat, having emerged from the path (magga), reviews the path; with the knowledge of others' minds, he knows the mind of one possessed of the mind leading to the cessation of rebirth; the aggregates leading to the cessation of rebirth are a condition for the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the future, and advertence (āvajjana) by way of object condition. (2)

A state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation is a condition for a state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation by way of object condition: An Arahat reviews the fruition (phala), reviews Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for fruition and for advertence by way of object condition. An Arahat contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; the ear... [pe]... the base... contemplates the aggregates that are neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; with the divine eye (dibbacakkhu), he sees a visible object; with the divine ear-element (dibbasotadhātu), he hears a sound; with the knowledge of others' minds, he knows the mind of one possessed of the mind that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation; the functional sphere of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatana-kiriya) is a condition for the functional sphere of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatana-kiriya) by way of object condition. The functional sphere of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatana-kiriya) is a condition for the functional sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatana-kiriya)... [pe]... the visible object base (rūpāyatana) is a condition for eye-consciousness (cakkhuviññāṇa)... [pe]... the tangible object base (phoṭṭhabbāyatana) is a condition for body-consciousness (kāyaviññāṇa)... [pe]... the aggregates that are neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers (iddhividhañāṇa), the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the future, and advertence by way of object condition. (1)

A state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation is a condition for a state leading to accumulation (ācayagāmī) by way of object condition: Sekkhas review the fruition, review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and for purification (vodāna) by way of object condition. Sekkhas or worldlings (puthujjanas) contemplate the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they enjoy it and delight in it; taking it as an object, lust (rāga) arises... [pe]... displeasure (domanassa) arises. The ear... [pe]... the base... they contemplate the aggregates that are neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they enjoy them and delight in them; taking those aggregates as an object, lust arises, wrong view (diṭṭhi) arises, doubt (vicikicchā)... [pe]... restlessness (uddhacca)... [pe]... displeasure... [pe]... arises. With the divine eye, they see a visible object; with the divine ear-element, they hear a sound.

With the knowledge of others' minds, they know the mind of one possessed of the mind that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation; the aggregates that are neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of the future by way of object condition. (2)

A state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation is a condition for a state leading to the cessation of rebirth by way of object condition: Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of object condition. (3)

## Adhipatipaccayo

A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of predominance condition: object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati) and co-nascence-predominance (sahajātādhipati). Object-predominance: Having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews it, giving it weight; one reviews former good deeds well performed, giving them weight; having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna, giving it weight; one enjoys and delights in the aggregates leading to accumulation, giving them weight; giving them weight, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence-predominance: The predominance leading to accumulation is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of predominance condition. (1)

A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation by way of predominance condition. Co-nascence-predominance: The predominance leading to accumulation is a condition for mind-produced matter (cittaja-rūpa) by way of predominance condition. (2)

A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state leading to accumulation and for a state that is neither leading to accumulation nor to cessation by way of predominance condition. Co-nascence-predominance: The predominance leading to accumulation is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition. (3)

A state leading to the cessation of rebirth is a condition for a state leading to the cessation of rebirth by way of predominance condition. Co-nascence-predominance: The predominance leading to the cessation of rebirth is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of predominance condition. (1)

A state leading to the cessation of rebirth is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance: Sekkhas, having emerged from the path, review the path, giving it weight. (2)

Conascence-predominance—apacayagāmī predominance is related to mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhamma is related to apacayagāmī dhamma and nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma by way of predominance condition. Conascence-predominance—apacayagāmī predominance is related to associated aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition. (4)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma is related to nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma by way of predominance condition: object-predominance, conascence-predominance. Object-predominance—an Arahant reviews Fruition, giving it importance; reviews Nibbāna, giving it importance; Nibbāna is related to Fruition by way of predominance condition. Conascence-predominance—nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī predominance is related to associated aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma is related to ācayagāmī dhamma by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance—Sekhas review Fruition, giving it importance; review Nibbāna, giving it importance; Nibbāna is related to gotrabhū and vodāna by way of predominance condition. Giving importance to the eye, one enjoys it... etc... the base... giving importance to nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī aggregates, one enjoys and delights in them; giving importance to those aggregates, lust arises, wrong view arises. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma is related to apacayagāmī dhamma by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance—Nibbāna is related to the Path by way of predominance condition. (3)

## Anantara-paccayo

Ācayagāmī dhamma is related to ācayagāmī dhamma by way of proximity condition—preceding ācayagāmī aggregates are related to subsequent ācayagāmī aggregates by way of proximity condition. Adaptation (anuloma) is related to gotrabhū... adaptation is related to vodāna by way of proximity condition. (1)
263:
Ācayagāmī dhamma is related to apacayagāmī dhamma by way of proximity condition—gotrabhū is related to the Path... vodāna is related to the Path by way of proximity condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī dhamma is related to nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma by way of proximity condition—ācayagāmī aggregates are related to emergence (vuṭṭhāna) by way of proximity condition. The adaptation (anuloma) of Sekhas is related to fruition attainment; the neither-perception-nor-non-perception wholesome (kusalajhāna) of one emerging from cessation is related to fruition attainment by way of proximity condition. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhamma is related to nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma by way of proximity condition—the Path is related to Fruition by way of proximity condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma is related to nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma by way of proximity condition—preceding nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī aggregates are related to subsequent nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī aggregates by way of proximity condition. Life-continuum (bhavaṅga) is related to advertence (āvajjana)... functional (kiriya) is related to emergence (vuṭṭhāna)... the adaptation of an Arahant is related to fruition attainment... the neither-perception-nor-non-perception functional (kiriyajhāna) of one emerging from cessation is related to fruition attainment by way of proximity condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhamma is related to ācayagāmī dhamma by way of proximity condition—advertence is related to ācayagāmī aggregates by way of proximity condition. (2)

## Upanissaya-paccayo

Ācayagāmī dhamma is related to ācayagāmī dhamma by way of decisive support condition—there are object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural-decisive support... etc. Natural-decisive support—depending on ācayagāmī faith, one gives gifts, observes virtue... etc... performs the uposatha... etc... jhāna... etc... insight... etc... direct knowledge... etc...
264:
...gives rise to attainment, manifests pride, takes up wrong view. Depending on ācayagāmī virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom, lust, hatred, delusion, pride, wrong view, and aspiration (patthanā), one gives gifts. One observes virtue, performs the uposatha, gives rise to jhāna, insight, direct knowledge, and attainment. One kills living beings, causes a schism in the Saṅgha. ## Root Condition
A learner state is related to a learner state by way of root condition: learner roots are related to the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (1)

## Object Condition
A learner state is related to a neither-learner-nor-non-learner state by way of object condition: noble ones, having emerged from the Path, review the Path; they review the learner Fruit; with the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, they know the mind of a person possessed of a learner mind; learner aggregates are related to the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, to the knowledge of recollection of past lives, to the knowledge of the future, and to advertence by way of object condition. (1)

An arahant state is related to a neither-learner-nor-non-learner state by way of object condition: an Arahant reviews the arahant Fruit; with the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, he knows the mind of a person possessed of an arahant mind; arahant aggregates are related to the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, to the knowledge of recollection of past lives, to the knowledge of the future, and to advertence by way of object condition. (1)
291:
A neither-learner-nor-non-learner state is related to a neither-learner-nor-non-learner state by way of object condition: having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the Uposatha duties, one reviews that merit; [one reviews] those things well-practiced in the past... having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna; noble ones review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage, to purification, and to advertence by way of object condition. Noble ones review the defilements that have been abandoned; they review the defilements abandoned by suppression; they know the defilements that occurred in the past; they contemplate the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they enjoy it, they delight in it; taking it as an object, lust arises... grief arises; the ear... the physical base... they contemplate neither-learner-nor-non-learner aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they enjoy them... grief arises; with the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear-element, one hears a sound; with the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, one knows the mind of a person possessed of a neither-learner-nor-non-learner mind; the sphere of infinite space is related to the sphere of infinite consciousness... the sphere of nothingness is related to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object condition. The visible form base is related to eye-consciousness... the tangible object base is related to body-consciousness... neither-learner-nor-non-learner aggregates are related to the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power, to the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, to the knowledge of recollection of past lives, to the knowledge of passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, to the knowledge of the future, and to advertence by way of object condition. (1)

A neither-learner-nor-non-learner state is related to a learner state by way of object condition: Nibbāna is related to the Path and to the learner Fruit by way of object condition. (2)

A neither-learner-nor-non-learner state is related to an arahant state by way of object condition: Nibbāna is related to the arahant Fruit by way of object condition. (3)
